profile.state: Red team engagement in progress

stimuli.title: Choosing how the machine decides
stimuli.text: Brackley Retail Group has heavy seasonal turnover and wants store associates' access created and removed automatically from HR job codes, so every cashier receives an identical, pre-approved bundle of permissions on day one. A review of the outgoing platform found that store managers had accumulated rights far beyond their duties, because every technician on the old console held full administrative powers regardless of what the job required. Millions of login attempts are arriving daily across thousands of usernames, one or two password tries each, from a rotating botnet, and many pairs match a recent third-party breach dump.

profile.environment: Heavy seasonal turnover · store associate accounts created from HR job codes
profile.state: Access model being selected for the new platform

stimuli.title: Letting a partner in without a password
stimuli.text: Brackley Retail Group wants employees to open a partner-hosted benefits portal from their browsers using their existing corporate directory logins, with the partner receiving no corporate passwords at any point, and the architecture board must pick the standard designed for exactly that. Its own directory is centralized for network access, and an engineer must centralize wireless and remote-access authentication so every connection attempt is validated against it with per-session accounting captured for chargeback. Employee representatives have objected to a proposed eye-based biometric on the grounds that scans could reveal medical conditions to the employer.

profile.environment: Partner-hosted benefits portal · corporate directory as identity provider
profile.state: Federation design being chosen

stimuli.title: Tokens, clocks and what a token proves
stimuli.text: Help-desk tickets at Kelvin Mutual spiked after a hypervisor migration: every six-digit code from users' authenticator apps is rejected by one of the two authentication servers while the same codes validate against its peer. The platform team must also settle how device administration is authenticated, wanting every typed command individually authorized against the operator's profile with the whole exchange encrypted. A consumer web application has separately been found treating possession of a bare access token as proof of identity: any valid token presented to the interface logs that bearer in as the user.

profile.environment: Two authentication servers behind a load balancer · one migrated to a new hypervisor
profile.state: Help-desk tickets spiking after a migration

stimuli.title: Labels, owners and rules
stimuli.text: Thorne Defense Systems is implementing a document system that must enforce government classification markings, with the operating system imposing every access decision so that no file owner can override or reclassify on their own authority. An auditor has separately found that spreadsheets holding cardholder data on a Windows file share were readable company-wide because their creators granted everyone read access on their own initiative. A shoulder-surfing concern has been raised about which of two token types leaves a glimpsed code useful for the shortest time, and a portal locks accounts after three failed logins.

profile.environment: Operating system enforces classification markings · file shares with owner-set permissions
profile.state: Two access models being compared

stimuli.title: Deciding on more than who you are
stimuli.text: Thorne Defense Systems wants console sessions permitted only when a technician connects from the corporate network, during a scheduled maintenance window, from a managed laptop that passes a patch-level check, and the policy engine must evaluate all of those together. The company is also moving domain logons to smart cards so that initial authentication uses certificate-based public key cryptography instead of a password-derived key. A consumer site already enforcing a second factor is receiving millions of automated credential-stuffing attempts daily from rotating residential proxies, and genuine login latency is degrading.

profile.environment: Console sessions restricted by network, time window and device posture
profile.state: Policy engine being specified

stimuli.title: Keys, cabinets and standing privilege
stimuli.text: Dunmore Cash Services keeps its safe master keys in an unlocked drawer that any office visitor could reach, and must bring physical key handling into line with the way it now controls logical access. It is evaluating privileged access management platforms, having found that anonymous use of a shared administrative account destroyed accountability. Its service desk provisions new hires by copying the account of a colleague on the same team, including group memberships that colleague accumulated over years. A benefits portal is separately being federated to a partner using browser-based assertions.

profile.organization: Dunmore Cash Services · vault and console operations
profile.environment: Safe master keys in an unlocked drawer · privileged access platform being evaluated
profile.state: Physical and logical key handling under review

stimuli.title: Two people, two halves
stimuli.text: Dunmore Cash Services requires that its safes open only under dual control, and the redesign has to satisfy that principle genuinely instead of in name. A separate vault combination is split so that each of two senior officers memorizes only half, and policy forbids either from ever learning the other. An application security review has found a portal authenticating users by simple bind to the corporate directory over an unprotected port, sending every username and password across the data-center network in clear. A bookkeeper has declined leave for four years.

profile.environment: Vault combination split between two officers · directory bind over an unprotected port
profile.state: Dual control being formalized

stimuli.title: One person who knows how it works
stimuli.text: An operations review at Dunmore Cash Services finds that a single administrator is the only person who understands the payment batch system, and auditors add that this concentration has let unexplained adjustments go unchallenged for years. A review of the monitoring software's service account separately finds it holds domain administrator rights, with login records showing technicians signing in with it interactively for day-to-day troubleshooting. The company is migrating workforce authentication to a cloud identity provider, and investigators have reconstructed how fabricated customer records with inflated limits were entered before any withdrawal was made.

profile.environment: One administrator understands the batch system · service account with domain rights
profile.state: Audit findings requiring response

stimuli.title: Oakhaven and the fall intake
stimuli.text: Oakhaven Claims Services settles auto claims for eleven insurers and hires 400 seasonal adjusters each fall, most of whom never visit an office. Recruiting collects a scanned driver's license by email and a manager's word that the person exists; a directory account and a laptop follow within a day. Adjusters sign in to the claims platform through Oakhaven's own identity provider, and three of the eleven insurers accept that assertion to open their portals. Team membership is copied from whichever adjuster the new hire is said to resemble. Two adjusters promoted to fraud review in March still hold the payment-release right they carried as adjusters. The fall intake starts in five weeks.

profile.organization: Oakhaven Claims Services · auto claims handling for eleven insurers
profile.regime: State insurance regulation · SOC 2 Type II for insurer clients
profile.environment: Cloud claims platform · own identity provider federated to three insurer portals
profile.state: Five weeks to a seasonal intake of 400 remote adjusters

stimuli.title: Saltmarsh turns on the access gateway
stimuli.text: Saltmarsh Securities runs an online brokerage for 90,000 retail customers and 340 staff. A new access gateway sits in front of the trading platform, the settlement system and the customer records database, and each of those applications still carries its own permission table. The gateway can call an external policy service before it forwards a request, and it can read device posture, geolocation and time of day. Customer web sessions last twelve hours and stay valid after a password change. Compliance requires that trades over $50,000 be entered from a managed workstation on the corporate network. The gateway has run for three weeks in monitor-only mode, and the platform team must decide what it should enforce.

profile.organization: Saltmarsh Securities · online brokerage, 90,000 retail customers
profile.regime: SEC and FINRA supervision · PCI DSS 4.0 for card funding
profile.environment: Access gateway fronting trading, settlement and customer records
profile.state: Gateway live three weeks in monitor-only mode

stimuli.title: Kentmere and the identities that are not people
stimuli.text: Kentmere Utilities meters 210,000 homes and equips 900 field crew with rugged tablets that read meters over Bluetooth and sync to the billing platform each evening. Any tablet presenting a valid crew password syncs, whether or not it is one of the 900. The customer mobile app authenticates to the same billing API with a key compiled into the app, and that key has been unchanged for three years. Overnight, a meter-data service pulls consumption records using a static API key held in a scheduled task, and the account behind that key has full read and write access to the billing database. Nobody at Kentmere can say which team owns the account.

profile.organization: Kentmere Utilities · water utility metering 210,000 homes
profile.regime: State utility commission · AWIA Section 2013 risk and resilience
profile.environment: 900 rugged field tablets · customer mobile app · billing API · overnight meter-data service
profile.state: Static keys in production, service account unowned

questions.question: The console is reachable from any office workstation and from the technicians' home connections. Which change BEST treats the console itself, and not its accounts, as the protected asset?

options.A: Requiring a second authentication factor from every technician who signs in to the console.
options.B: Reviewing the console's account list each quarter and removing accounts no longer needed.
options.C: Admitting console sessions through one managed access point that mediates and records them.
options.D: Encrypting console session traffic so credentials stay unreadable on the office network.

questions.explanation:
The console answers from any office workstation and from the technicians' home connections. That is a property of the system. Work on its accounts leaves it exactly where it is.
Routing every session through one managed access point (C) changes it. NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AC-17(3) Remote Access | Managed Access Control Points requires remote access to be routed through a defined number of managed network access control points. AC-3 Access Enforcement locates enforcement inside the system itself. The single mediated path also gives you one place to watch.
Ask what the asset is before you choose the control.
questions.recallLine: An administration console answers from anywhere. What treats the console, not its accounts, as the asset?

optionsShort.A: Second factor for technicians
optionsShort.B: Quarterly account list review
optionsShort.C: One managed access point for sessions
optionsShort.D: Encrypt console session traffic

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Strengthens the sign-in event the stem deliberately sets aside. The console still answers from everywhere it answered before.

B.label: detective when preventive is asked
B.wouldAnswer: Detective where the question asks for preventive. It finds a stale account a quarter after it stopped being needed.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: Protects the traffic in flight. The exposure is the set of places the console will answer.

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | AC-17(3) Remote Access | Managed Access Control Points
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | AC-3 Access Enforcement

questions.question: QuickCash wants staff to sign in to the two cloud applications with their existing directory accounts, and the directory will stay in the regional office. Which element MOST determines whether that federation is trustworthy?

options.A: Whether the identity provider runs on the firm's own hardware or on a hosted platform.
options.B: Whether the assertion travels over a channel encrypted end to end between the parties.
options.C: Whether each application can read the full set of attributes held in the directory.
options.D: Whether the terms each party is trusted for are agreed and documented before the first sign-in.

questions.explanation:
Federation is a transfer of belief. What makes it safe is that both sides wrote down what they were believing before the first sign-in (D).
NIST SP 800-63C-4 Section 3.5 Trust Agreements states that all federation transactions shall be governed by the terms of one or more trust agreements between the applicable parties. It enumerates the relationships those terms cover, including what the relying party trusts the identity provider to represent and what the identity provider trusts the relying party to do with the attributes released. Section 3.2 defines the roles the agreement binds.
One useful caution. SP 800-63C-4's own two models are general-purpose identity providers and subscriber-controlled wallets, at Section 3.1. The on-premise, cloud and hybrid split is the exam outline's deployment framing, and the trust-agreement obligation is identical wherever the provider runs.
Write down what you are trusting.
questions.recallLine: Staff will sign in to cloud applications using an on-premises directory. What most determines trustworthiness?

optionsShort.A: Own hardware or hosted platform
optionsShort.B: End-to-end encrypted assertion channel
optionsShort.C: Applications read all directory attributes
optionsShort.D: Documented trust agreement terms first

A.label: symptom not cause
A.wouldAnswer: Decides who operates the provider. Whether the trust was ever established is a separate question, and it is the one asked.

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Protects the assertion. One from an untrusted issuer is still untrusted, however well protected.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: One clause inside the agreement, and released in full, a bad one.

sources: NIST SP 800-63C-4 | Section 3.5 Trust Agreements; Section 3.2 Roles; Section 3.1 Federation Models
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | IA-8 Identification and Authentication (Non-Organizational Users); SA-9 External System Services

questions.question: QuickCash's card-data extract is copied nightly from the console to an analyst's laptop, then into a spreadsheet on a shared drive. Access is controlled separately on each of the three systems. Which control BEST protects the information itself as it moves?

options.A: Requiring the same group membership on all three systems before access is granted.
options.B: Encrypting each system's storage so the extract is unreadable if a disk is removed.
options.C: Labeling the extract and enforcing flow rules that follow the label between systems.
options.D: Reviewing the three systems' access lists on the same quarterly cycle.

questions.explanation:
Three well-controlled systems can still add up to an uncontrolled dataset. The extract sheds its protection at every boundary and picks up whatever the next system happens to grant.
A label that travels with the data, and flow rules that honor it (C), survive the crossing. NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AC-4 Information Flow Enforcement requires approved authorizations to be enforced for controlling the flow of information within the system and between connected systems. AC-16 Security and Privacy Attributes supplies the binding that makes that possible, associating attributes with information and enforcing decisions on the basis of them. Together they are the catalog's answer to information as an access-control asset class, distinct from the system-by-system enforcement in AC-3.
Control the data as well as the doors.
questions.recallLine: A card-data extract crosses three separately controlled systems. What protects the information itself?

optionsShort.A: Same groups on all three systems
optionsShort.B: Encrypt storage on each system
optionsShort.C: Label the data, enforce flow rules
optionsShort.D: Aligned quarterly access reviews

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: Harmonizes three per-system decisions. The data still crosses unattended between them.

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Protects media at rest. A copy in motion is the exposure here.

D.label: detective when preventive is asked
D.wouldAnswer: Detective where preventive is asked, and it reads who may reach each system. Where the data went is a different record.

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | AC-4 Information Flow Enforcement; AC-16 Security and Privacy Attributes
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | AC-3 Access Enforcement

questions.question: Which failure in the identification, authentication, authorization and accounting chain is the PRIMARY cause of the inability to attribute?

options.A: Authentication - the account was protected by a single weak password
options.B: Identification - five people operated the console under one user identity
options.C: Authorization - the account held far more rights than technicians needed
options.D: Accountability - the console failed to log administrative sessions

questions.explanation:
Five people operated the console under one user identity (B). The log could name that identity and nothing further, so it could never name a person. Perfect logging would have changed nothing.
The weak password, the excessive rights and the thin record are all real faults in this environment, and none of them is the reason the investigator cannot name an actor. That failure happened at identification, upstream of all three.
Accountability can only ever be as granular as identification. Unique identities are the foundation the rest of IAAA stands on.
questions.recallLine: Five technicians share one administrative console account, and no withdrawal can be tied to a person. Which IAAA element's failure is the PRIMARY cause?

optionsShort.A: Authentication: one weak password protected it
optionsShort.B: Identification: five people, one user identity
optionsShort.C: Authorization: rights far exceeded technician need
optionsShort.D: Accountability: console failed to log sessions

A.label: wrong phase
A.wouldAnswer: Real enough. 'Welcome123!' with no MFA made entry easy, and a strong shared account still leaves five suspects.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Also true here. Excessive rights widened what the insider could do, which goes to impact and not to attribution.

D.label: symptom not cause
D.wouldAnswer: Misreads the evidence. Sessions were logged; the record said 'SuperAdmin logged in', so the logging itself worked.

questions.question: Which attack technique is MOST likely to still succeed against the upgraded webmail login?

options.A: Credential stuffing that replays username and password pairs harvested from breaches of unrelated services
options.B: Offline cracking of stolen password hashes using precomputed tables
options.C: A scripted brute-force loop guessing all possible six-digit codes against the login endpoint
options.D: A proxy page that captures and instantly relays both the password and current code

questions.explanation:
A TOTP code is bound to a clock and to nothing about the site the user typed it into. A proxy page can therefore capture the password and the current code and relay both to the real service inside the validity window (D). The upgrade does not touch that flow.
OTP-based MFA raises the bar and stays phishable in real time. Closing that gap takes an origin-bound, phishing-resistant method such as FIDO2/WebAuthn.
questions.recallLine: Webmail now requires an app-generated time-based code after employees were phished. Which attack technique is MOST likely to still succeed?

optionsShort.A: Credential stuffing with pairs from other breaches
optionsShort.B: Offline hash cracking with precomputed tables
optionsShort.C: Brute-forcing every six-digit code
optionsShort.D: Proxy page relaying password and live code

A.label: wrong phase
A.wouldAnswer: Credential stuffing now fails, because a stolen password alone no longer completes a login.

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Yields passwords and then meets the same second-factor wall.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: Dies on the 30-second code lifetime combined with ordinary attempt throttling.

questions.question: Which control would MOST reliably have surfaced that accumulation of entitlements earlier?

options.A: SIEM alerting tuned to anomalous use of the finance applications
options.B: Periodic recertification of each user's entitlements by their manager
options.C: A stronger multi-factor policy on all finance system logins
options.D: Automated birthright provisioning for employees joining the firm

questions.explanation:
Privilege creep is a condition of the account. The excess rights sit there whether or not anyone exercises them, so the control that finds them has to compare periodically what a person holds against what their current role needs. Manager-driven recertification (B) does exactly that, which is why it catches accumulation from transfers.
Reviews audit entitlement state; monitoring audits behavior. Creep hides in the first, so schedule recertification around transfers.
questions.recallLine: An employee who transferred three times can approve invoices, edit vendor records and view payroll. Which control would MOST reliably surface that accumulation earlier?

optionsShort.A: SIEM alerts on anomalous finance-application use
optionsShort.B: Managers periodically recertify each user's entitlements
optionsShort.C: Stronger MFA on finance system logins
optionsShort.D: Automated birthright provisioning for new joiners

A.label: symptom not cause
A.wouldAnswer: Watches usage. Dormant excess rights fire no events to alert on.

C.label: wrong phase
C.wouldAnswer: Makes it more certain the right person is behind the login. Whether that login should hold those rights goes unasked.

D.label: wrong phase
D.wouldAnswer: Governs the joiner moment. This risk was created by moves, the lifecycle phase birthright provisioning never revisits.

questions.question: Which figure gives the fairest single basis for comparing the three products?

options.A: The lowest false acceptance rate that each vendor quotes in its datasheet
options.B: The false rejection rate each vendor measured during its own pilot
options.C: The failure-to-enroll rate observed across the user population
options.D: The crossover error rate, where false accepts and false rejects are equal

questions.explanation:
FAR and FRR both move with the threshold, so a vendor can make either number look excellent by choosing where to measure. The crossover error rate (D) removes that freedom. It fixes the comparison at the setting where the two rates meet, so a lower CER means a genuinely more accurate sensor.
Compare products at a fixed point on the curve. Tune to the site's risk bias afterward, once the product is chosen.
questions.recallLine: Three fingerprint vendors quote error rates measured at thresholds each chose. Which figure gives the fairest single basis for comparing the products?

optionsShort.A: Lowest false acceptance rate each vendor quotes
optionsShort.B: False rejection rate from each vendor's pilot
optionsShort.C: Failure-to-enroll rate across the user population
optionsShort.D: Crossover error rate, where both rates meet

A.label: wrong phase
A.wouldAnswer: One end of a tunable trade. Quoted alone it is a marketing figure, useful again only when tuning the sensor you picked.

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: The other end of the same trade, measured on the vendor's own pilot, at whatever threshold flattered the product.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Measures how many users can register at all. It says nothing about matching accuracy once a user is enrolled.

questions.question: Now that one login unlocks everything, which recommendation about protecting the portal credential is MOST appropriate?

options.A: Rotate the retired downstream application passwords on a shorter schedule
options.B: Keep separate standalone passwords for the three most sensitive applications
options.C: Require phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication at the portal login
options.D: Extend the portal session lifetime so users authenticate less often

questions.explanation:
Single sign-on concentrates authentication risk on purpose. Convenience rises, and the portal credential becomes the key to the kingdom, so that one credential has to be hardened to a level none of the forty passwords ever needed. Phishing-resistant MFA at the portal (C) is that level.
When one login opens everything, spend the protection where the concentration is.
questions.recallLine: Forty applications now sit behind one sign-on portal. Which recommendation about protecting the portal credential is MOST appropriate?

optionsShort.A: Rotate retired downstream application passwords faster
optionsShort.B: Keep standalone passwords for three sensitive applications
optionsShort.C: Require phishing-resistant multi-factor at the portal
optionsShort.D: Extend session lifetime so users authenticate less

A.label: wrong phase
A.wouldAnswer: Polishes credentials that single sign-on has taken off the attack path.

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: Quietly abandons single sign-on for the crown jewels, and multiplies user friction to do it.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Moves the wrong way, lengthening the window a hijacked session stays valid.

questions.question: Which process change MOST directly ends a departing employee's access before the termination window opens?

options.A: Trigger automatic account suspension from HR termination workflow events
options.B: Add a quarterly manager recertification of every technician's access
options.C: Shorten the maximum password age on privileged accounts to thirty days
options.D: Collect badges, tokens and master keys during each exit interview

questions.explanation:
The gap is timing. The organization knew the termination was coming before the employee did. Only an automated feed from the HR termination workflow (A) turns that knowledge into disabled access at the right moment, uniformly across every site.
Deprovisioning is an event. Wire identity systems to HR triggers so access dies the moment trust does.
questions.recallLine: The bank knows a technician is being terminated before he does. Which process change MOST directly ends his access in that window?

optionsShort.A: Automatic suspension from HR termination workflow events
optionsShort.B: Quarterly manager recertification of technician access
optionsShort.C: Thirty-day maximum password age on privileged accounts
optionsShort.D: Collect badges and tokens at exit interview

B.label: detective when preventive is asked
B.wouldAnswer: The correct tool for finding quietly accumulated rights. A quarterly cadence can trail a termination by months.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Rotates a credential the departing insider legitimately holds until the rotation lands. It narrows stale secrets instead.

D.label: wrong phase
D.wouldAnswer: Recovers physical credentials at or after the exit conversation, inside the window the lead wants closed, and touches nothing logical.

questions.question: Which password storage design BEST resists offline cracking the next time a table is stolen?

options.A: Unsalted SHA-512 digests, substituting a longer modern hash for MD5
options.B: Per-user salts fed into a slow, memory-hard function such as Argon2
options.C: AES-encrypted passwords with the key kept in the application's config file
options.D: Salted MD5 digests, retaining the fast algorithm but defeating rainbow tables

questions.explanation:
Offline cracking is an economics problem, and per-user salts fed into a slow, memory-hard function such as Argon2 (B) attack both of its terms. Unique salts force the attacker to work one user at a time, with no precomputed tables. A deliberately slow, memory-hard function cuts guessing from billions per second to thousands. NIST SP 800-63B prescribes this approach for memorized secrets.
Break precomputation, then raise the price of every remaining guess.
questions.recallLine: Brackley must redesign password storage so the next stolen table resists offline cracking. Which storage design BEST achieves that?

optionsShort.A: Unsalted SHA-512, a longer modern digest
optionsShort.B: Per-user salts into a slow memory-hard function
optionsShort.C: AES encryption, key in the application config
optionsShort.D: Salted MD5, fast but rainbow-table proof

A.label: symptom not cause
A.wouldAnswer: Swaps one fast, unsalted digest for another. SHA-512's extra bits do nothing against lookup tables or GPU throughput.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Makes passwords recoverable by design, and whoever stole the database plausibly holds the config file key too.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: Half the fix. The salt kills precomputation; MD5's speed still permits enormous per-user guessing rates.

questions.question: A scheduling app must read users' calendars at a third-party provider without ever seeing their passwords. Which framework should the team implement?

options.A: OAuth 2.0, so each user authorizes a scoped access token for the app
options.B: OpenID Connect, so the app receives a signed ID token identifying each authenticated user
options.C: SAML 2.0, so the provider asserts each user's authentication to the app
options.D: Kerberos delegation, so the app forwards each user's service tickets

questions.explanation:
The requirement is delegated authorization: let this app read my calendar, nothing more, and never show it my password. That is OAuth 2.0's exact purpose (A). The user consents at the provider, and the app receives an access token limited to the calendar scope.
OAuth answers what may this app touch. OIDC and SAML answer who is this user.
questions.recallLine: A scheduling app must read users' calendars at a third-party provider without ever seeing their passwords. Which framework should the team implement?

optionsShort.A: OAuth 2.0: user authorizes a scoped token
optionsShort.B: OpenID Connect: signed ID token naming the user
optionsShort.C: SAML 2.0: provider asserts the user's authentication
optionsShort.D: Kerberos delegation: app forwards the user's tickets

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Tells the app who the user is. Identity alone confers no right to read resource data.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Asserts authentication between organizations and carries no resource-scoped delegation for an API.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: An intra-domain mechanism for services acting on a user's behalf inside one Kerberos realm, not a pattern across providers.

questions.question: Which cause should the engineer investigate FIRST for the rejected codes?

options.A: Clock drift on the migrated server breaking time-step agreement
options.B: Counter desynchronization between the apps and the server
options.C: Corrupted shared seeds requiring re-enrollment of every authenticator
options.D: An expired TLS certificate on the affected validation endpoint

questions.explanation:
TOTP validation computes a code from the shared seed and the current 30-second time step, so both ends have to agree on the time. A virtual machine migration is a classic way for one guest's clock to drift while its peer stays true. Clock drift on the migrated server (A) matches the evidence exactly: same users, same seeds, one server rejecting.
When one validator rejects what another accepts, suspect whatever differs between them. For TOTP that is almost always the clock.
questions.recallLine: After a hypervisor migration, one authentication server rejects every authenticator code its peer accepts. Which cause should the engineer investigate FIRST?

optionsShort.A: Clock drift breaking time-step agreement
optionsShort.B: Counter desynchronization between apps and server
optionsShort.C: Corrupted seeds requiring re-enrollment of every authenticator
optionsShort.D: Expired TLS certificate on the validation endpoint

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: Describes HOTP, the counter-based variant. A counter problem would follow the user from one server to the other.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: Cannot explain codes validating on the peer. Both servers verify against the same seeds, so corruption would fail everywhere.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Would stop clients connecting or raise certificate errors. The engineer is seeing a clean rejection of well-formed codes.

questions.question: Which access control model fits the requirement that no file owner may override or reclassify?

options.A: Role-based access control driven by job assignments
options.B: Discretionary access control administered by resource owners
options.C: Mandatory access control enforced through security labels
options.D: Attribute-based access control evaluating contextual rules

questions.explanation:
Two phrases in the stem decide it: classification markings, and decisions imposed by the system beyond any owner's authority. That pair defines mandatory access control (C), where subjects hold clearances, objects hold labels, and policy is centrally enforced.
Read the stem for who decides. Labels the system imposes, with no owner override, name one model only.
questions.recallLine: A document system must enforce government classification markings so that no file owner can reclassify. Which access control model fits that requirement?

optionsShort.A: Role-based, driven by job assignments
optionsShort.B: Discretionary, administered by resource owners
optionsShort.C: Mandatory, enforced through security labels
optionsShort.D: Attribute-based, evaluating contextual rules

A.label: not the decision-maker's
A.wouldAnswer: Grants by job function, and an administrator can still adjust assignments, which the requirement excludes.

B.label: not the decision-maker's
B.wouldAnswer: The direct opposite of the requirement. Owner discretion is exactly what has to be removed.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Could emulate labels among its attributes. Its purpose is dynamic, condition-based decisions, which is a different shape.

questions.question: Which characteristic of the file share environment made the company-wide readability possible?

options.A: Rule-based control applies one uniform policy to every subject
options.B: Discretionary control leaves grant decisions with each resource owner
options.C: Mandatory control ties every access decision to clearance levels
options.D: Role-based control links permissions to defined job functions

questions.explanation:
Windows NTFS permissions follow the discretionary model (B). Whoever owns a file may share it at will, so a well-meaning creator can quietly grant the world access to regulated data. That owner discretion is the mechanism the auditor observed.
DAC's convenience is its risk. Owner-controlled sharing scales into sprawl unless it is monitored, or replaced for sensitive data.
questions.recallLine: Cardholder spreadsheets on a Windows share were readable company-wide. Which characteristic of that file share environment made that possible?

optionsShort.A: Rule-based: one uniform policy for every subject
optionsShort.B: Discretionary: owners decide their own grants
optionsShort.C: Mandatory: decisions tied to clearance levels
optionsShort.D: Role-based: permissions linked to job functions

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: Describes system-wide rules such as firewall-style conditions. Under one uniform policy the creator could not have loosened it.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Would have made the oversharing impossible, since labels and clearances remove the owner's choice. A different environment.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: Would bound access by job function. The finding shows access following individual grant decisions.

questions.question: Which replacement practice would BEST bring physical key handling into line with identity principles?

options.A: Issue keys individually from an audited cabinet with per-person sign-out records
options.B: Install a camera covering the key storage area so removals can be reviewed
options.C: Move the keys into a locked cabinet whose combination all technicians share
options.D: Remove the identifying label so the keys' purpose is hidden from a visitor

questions.explanation:
Physical keys are credentials. The case study's core lesson - one identity per person, with attributable use - reaches them just as it reaches logins. An audited cabinet with per-person sign-out (A) restores identification and accountability for every key movement.
Treat a key the way you treat an account. Issue it to one person, and keep a record of who holds it.
questions.recallLine: Safe master keys sit in an unlocked drawer any office visitor could reach. Which replacement practice BEST aligns key handling with identity principles?

optionsShort.A: Audited cabinet with per-person sign-out records
optionsShort.B: Camera covering the key storage area
optionsShort.C: Locked cabinet with a shared combination
optionsShort.D: Remove the label identifying what keys open

B.label: detective when preventive is asked
B.wouldAnswer: Purely detective. Footage may show who took a key after the cash has gone.

C.label: symptom not cause
C.wouldAnswer: Upgrades the container and recreates the SuperAdmin defect in physical form. A shared combination is a shared credential.

D.label: symptom not cause
D.wouldAnswer: Security through obscurity. An unlabeled unlocked drawer is still an uncontrolled credential store.

questions.question: Which risk does the split-knowledge arrangement MOST directly address?

options.A: A single trusted insider misusing the complete secret alone
options.B: Losing access to the vault when one officer resigns abruptly
options.C: Disclosure of the combination while it is first distributed
options.D: Systematic manipulation of the vault's mechanical dial

questions.explanation:
Split the secret and no individual ever holds enough to act. Exploiting the vault now takes collusion between two trusted people (A), a far rarer event than one insider going bad - as the QuickCash case shows.
Splitting a secret buys collusion resistance and costs availability. Both belong in the recommendation.
questions.recallLine: Two officers each memorize half a vault combination and neither may learn the other. Which risk does that split-knowledge arrangement MOST directly address?

optionsShort.A: A lone insider misusing the whole secret
optionsShort.B: Losing vault access when an officer resigns
optionsShort.C: Disclosure while the combination is first distributed
optionsShort.D: Manipulation of the vault's mechanical dial

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: Gets the effect backwards. Split knowledge worsens availability, since a departed officer takes an irreplaceable half.

C.label: wrong phase
C.wouldAnswer: Untouched. Each half still has to reach its officer somehow, and a distribution channel can leak either one.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Concerns the lock's physical attack resistance, which no knowledge-management arrangement changes.

questions.question: Which remediation BEST addresses both findings on the service account?

options.A: Rotate the service account password and store it in the team's vault
options.B: Rename the account to obscure its function from observers
options.C: Enroll the service account in the company's standard MFA program
options.D: Scope the account to minimum required rights and block interactive logon

questions.explanation:
The review surfaced two defects: excessive privilege, and human use of a machine identity. The remediation has to close both. Least-privilege scoping removes the domain-admin blast radius, and blocking interactive logon pushes technicians back onto their own accounts, restoring attribution (D).
Two findings need a remediation that closes both. Check the second one before accepting an answer that closes the first.
questions.recallLine: A monitoring service account holds domain administrator rights, and technicians sign in with it interactively. Which remediation BEST addresses both findings?

optionsShort.A: Rotate the password and vault it
optionsShort.B: Rename the account to obscure its function
optionsShort.C: Enroll the service account in standard MFA
optionsShort.D: Scope rights down and block interactive logon

A.label: correct but not first
A.wouldAnswer: Sound hygiene that leaves both findings standing. The freshly rotated secret still carries domain admin.

B.label: symptom not cause
B.wouldAnswer: Obscurity. An attacker enumerating privileged group membership finds the account whatever it is called.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Misfits the account type. Unattended software cannot answer an interactive MFA prompt.

questions.question: What must happen BEFORE a directory account is issued to a seasonal adjuster?

options.A: A manager's attestation that the applicant is genuine is recorded in the onboarding ticket.
options.B: The license is validated with the issuing authority and matched to the applicant.
options.C: A hardware authenticator is issued and bound to the adjuster at first sign-in.
options.D: An email verification link is sent and clicked to confirm the applicant's address.

questions.explanation:
Enrollment has an order, and the order is the control. NIST SP 800-63A resolves, validates and verifies the claimed identity; only then does SP 800-63B bind an authenticator to the subject that proofing produced. Validating the license with the issuing authority and matching it to the applicant (B) is what makes the resulting account refer to a human being.
Decide what an identity asserts before deciding how hard it is to steal.
questions.recallLine: Before a seasonal adjuster's account is created, which step establishes that the applicant is the person hired?

optionsShort.A: A manager's attestation filed in the ticket
optionsShort.B: Validate the license with the issuing authority
optionsShort.C: Bind a hardware authenticator at first sign-in
optionsShort.D: Click an emailed verification link

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Authorization to create the account. It is no evidence of who will hold it, and a hiring manager can be socially engineered.

C.label: wrong phase
C.wouldAnswer: Necessary, and later. Bind a token to an unproven identity and you get a well-protected fiction.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: Demonstrates control of an email address. Adequate for a newsletter, not for an adjuster who can release payments.

sources: NIST SP 800-63A-3 | §5 Identity Resolution, Validation, and Verification
NIST SP 800-63B-3 | §6.1 Authenticator Binding
ISC2 CISSP 2024 outline | 5.2.4

questions.question: Which mechanism MOST directly enforces the $50,000 condition without depending on who the trader is?

options.A: Grant a role to the traders who are authorized to place large orders.
options.B: Let each desk head decide at their discretion who may exceed the limit.
options.C: Deny orders above the threshold when the request comes from an unmanaged device.
options.D: Label orders and workstations by sensitivity and let the system compare the labels.

questions.explanation:
Access control models differ in what the decision is a function of. Role-based decisions are a function of the subject's job. Discretionary decisions are a function of an owner's choice. Mandatory decisions are a function of labels carried by subject and object. A rule-based decision is a function of the request's own attributes: amount, device state, network. Deny orders above the threshold from an unmanaged device (C) and the rule applies identically to the newest trader and to the head of the desk. That is what a compliance condition written about orders needs.
Read the requirement and ask what the decision has to be a function of.
questions.recallLine: A rule applies to every trade over a set amount regardless of the trader. Which access control model MOST directly expresses it?

optionsShort.A: A role for large-order traders
optionsShort.B: Desk heads waive the limit at discretion
optionsShort.C: Deny above-threshold orders from unmanaged devices
optionsShort.D: Compare sensitivity labels on orders and workstations

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Puts the condition on the person, so a trader holding the role keeps it on an unmanaged laptop at home.

B.label: not the decision-maker's
B.wouldAnswer: Makes the limit negotiable by the manager most motivated to waive it.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: Would work, and it imposes a labeling scheme across every order and workstation to express one threshold.

sources: NISTIR 7316 | Assessment of Access Control Systems, access control policy classes
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | AC-3 Access Enforcement
ISC2 CISSP 2024 outline | 5.4.2

questions.question: Which step should Kentmere take FIRST on the unowned overnight service account?

options.A: Rotate the key and move it into the platform team's secrets manager.
options.B: Move the scheduled task onto the hardened jump host the platform team maintains.
options.C: Ask the billing manager to approve the account at the quarterly access review.
options.D: Record the account in the service-account register with a named owning team.

questions.explanation:
A service credential nobody owns cannot be corrected safely. Every other step on this list needs someone who knows what breaks.
Recording the account in the service-account register with a named owning team (D) is what gives a credential a lifecycle. A team to right-size its rights. A team to answer at rotation time. A team to decommission it when the meter-data feed is retired. NIST SP 800-53 AC-2 assigns account managers for exactly that reason.
Give a non-human identity a human name before giving it anything else.
questions.recallLine: An overnight service account holds full read and write rights and has no owner. What should the utility do FIRST?

optionsShort.A: Rotate the key into a secrets manager
optionsShort.B: Run the task on a hardened host
optionsShort.C: Manager approves it at quarterly review
optionsShort.D: Register the account with a named owner

A.label: correct but not first
A.wouldAnswer: The second step, and a good one. Rotate a key whose consumers are unknown and the nightly billing run stops at two.

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Changes where the task executes and leaves a full read-write credential sitting in a scheduled job.

C.label: not the decision-maker's
C.wouldAnswer: Asks a manager who does not own the account to certify it, converting an unowned account into an approved unowned one.

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | AC-2 Account Management, account managers and account types
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | IA-5(7) Authenticator Management, no embedded unencrypted static authenticators
ISC2 CISSP 2024 outline | 5.1.6

domains.title: Security Assessment and Testing
domains.caseStudy:
Domain 6 is how you find out whether controls work: vulnerability assessment, penetration testing, code testing, log review, audits, and the metrics that tell management what the results mean.

Case Study: The "Unchecked Validator" Logic Bomb

### Context

FinCorp rushed a mobile check deposit feature for its ATM app to beat a competitor to market. Three weeks behind schedule, the VP of Engineering waived the security gate review and promised to fix anything found afterwards. The feature let a user type the check amount by hand.

### What went wrong

A researcher entered a negative amount. The balance logic subtracted the deposit as written: balance minus negative one hundred is balance plus one hundred. Money appeared from nothing.

Four things had to fail for that to ship. Functional testing covered the happy path and no edge cases, so nobody typed a minus sign. No static analysis ran, and a SAST tool would have flagged the unvalidated integer. The vulnerability scanner was running, but the new application server's IP range had been dropped from the scan scope during a firewall change. No penetration test was commissioned, and a tester with ten minutes and a sense of what a deposit should never do would have found it.

The ATM industry has its own business-logic flaw, and the white paper documents it under transaction reversal fraud. The criminal times a card-reader fault so the host reverses a withdrawal whose cash has already been staged, then forces the shutter. It works because the host's reversal logic trusts the wrong signal. No scanner finds that; it takes someone who understands the transaction state machine and tests it on purpose. The negative deposit is the same class of defect on the deposit side.

### What a practitioner does differently

The test plan carries negative, boundary and abuse cases, written from the question "what must this feature never do?" Static analysis runs in the build pipeline on every commit. Dynamic testing and a penetration test run against pre-production, with business-logic cases in the scope, not only the OWASP checklist.

Scan scope is tied to the asset inventory through change control, so the firewall change that moved the server also updated the scanner's targets. A gap in scope is a gap in coverage, and the metric that reports "no critical findings" is worthless if it silently excludes the newest system.

The security gate cannot be waived by the person who benefits from waiving it. A waiver is a risk acceptance: it is signed by the risk owner, recorded, time-boxed, and reviewed. And the researcher needs a door: a published disclosure policy so the report lands with security instead of on social media.

### Outcome

The researcher reported the flaw through a support address, and FinCorp closed it. The postmortem replaced "fix it in post" with a gate that only the risk owner can defer, and put the application server back in the scanner's scope.

### What the exam tests

Expect questions distinguishing assessment, audit and testing; SAST versus DAST versus manual review and what each can and cannot find; penetration-test phases and rules of engagement; misuse-case and negative testing; scan scope and coverage as management metrics; and who is allowed to accept a risk.

### Related reading

The firm in this scenario is a composite. The ATM analogue and the controls are documented in:

- [Technical Risks and Attack Vectors Targeting ATMs](https://portfolio.atmavailability.com/atm-technical-risks-white-paper.pdf), the sections on transaction reversal fraud and on monitoring, auditing and incident response (audits, vulnerability assessments, penetration tests).
- [ATM Security Capability Maturity Worksheet](https://portfolio.atmavailability.com/atm-capability-maturity-worksheet.pdf), Domain 4, process and governance controls.

stimuli.title: FinCorp: the second report
stimuli.text: FinCorp's mobile check deposit accepted a negative amount and credited the customer, and the story reached the press. Nine days later its security mailbox receives a second report. An independent researcher writes that the same mobile deposit endpoint accepts an amount carrying sixteen decimal places, and that the balance service rounds it in the customer's favor. She has not published, gives a ninety-day deadline, and asks for a named contact. FinCorp has no vulnerability disclosure policy, no bug bounty, and no stated position on researchers who test its live application. The VP of Engineering who waived the pre-release security review still owns the release schedule. Legal's first draft reply threatens action under the terms of service.

The team also wants the missing input-validation check flagged automatically in the build pipeline, before the application is ever deployed to a test server, and wants evidence the board can rank spending against.

stimuli.text: Thistlewood Mutual, a 900-employee insurer in Des Moines, sends one security metrics pack to its risk committee each quarter. questions.question: Legal's draft reply threatens action under the terms of service. What should the security lead advise FIRST?

options.A: Ask the researcher to sign a non-disclosure agreement before the report is examined.
options.B: Establish a published reporting channel with safe-harbor terms, then reply through it.
options.C: Refer the report to the card brands so they can direct FinCorp's response to it.
options.D: Reproduce the finding and patch it before any reply is sent to the researcher.

questions.explanation:
FinCorp has no route by which a report can arrive, so every reply it drafts is improvised. Improvised replies from Legal are how a ninety-day deadline becomes a press cycle.
Establish a published reporting channel with safe-harbor terms and answer through it (B). NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 RA-5(11) Vulnerability Monitoring and Scanning | Public Disclosure Program is the precise and rarely quoted control. It requires a public reporting channel for receiving reports of vulnerabilities in organizational systems and system components. NIST SP 800-218 RV.1.3 states the developer-side obligation, a policy addressing vulnerability disclosure and remediation with the roles and processes to support it. NIST SP 800-216 is the dedicated federal guideline on the subject.
Build the channel, then use it.
questions.recallLine: A researcher reports a live flaw and Legal drafts a threat. What should the security lead advise first?

optionsShort.A: Ask for a non-disclosure agreement
optionsShort.B: Publish a channel with safe harbor
optionsShort.C: Refer it to the card brands
optionsShort.D: Reproduce and patch before replying

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: The right control for a different problem. A non-disclosure agreement manages a paid engagement; this researcher owes nothing.

C.label: not the decision-maker's
C.wouldAnswer: Hands the reply to the card brands. FinCorp owns the system and owns the answer.

D.label: correct but not first
D.wouldAnswer: Correct, and later. The clock runs whether or not anyone answers, and a silent patch invites publication.

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | RA-5(11) Vulnerability Monitoring and Scanning | Public Disclosure Program
NIST SP 800-218 | RV.1.3 vulnerability disclosure and remediation policy
NIST SP 800-216 named as the dedicated federal disclosure guideline

questions.question: The finding is reproduced. The VP of Engineering proposes shipping the fix in the release already scheduled for eleven weeks out. Which response BEST reflects how remediation should be decided?

options.A: Ship in the scheduled release, because unscheduled changes carry risks of their own.
options.B: Ship immediately, because any confirmed defect in a money path is an emergency.
options.C: Ask the researcher whether she will extend the ninety-day deadline to cover the release.
options.D: Rank it against the other open findings by exploitability and impact, then set the date.

questions.explanation:
Remediation timing is a risk decision, and a risk decision needs a basis that survives being asked about later. Rank the finding against the other open ones by exploitability and impact, then set the date (D).
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 CA-5 Plan of Action and Milestones requires documented planned remediation actions to correct weaknesses noted during control assessments, with milestones. RA-7 Risk Response requires the organization to respond to findings in accordance with its own risk tolerance. NIST SP 800-115 Chapter 8, Post-Testing Activities, covers turning findings into mitigation recommendations and a remediation plan. Ranking is what lets FinCorp defend either a rushed fix or a scheduled one.
Decide by risk, then argue about the calendar.
questions.recallLine: When should a confirmed money-path defect be fixed, and on what basis is that decided?

optionsShort.A: Wait for the scheduled release
optionsShort.B: Ship immediately as an emergency
optionsShort.C: Ask for a deadline extension
optionsShort.D: Rank by exploitability and impact

A.label: not the decision-maker's
A.wouldAnswer: Treats ownership of the release calendar as though it settled a risk question.

B.label: correct but not first
B.wouldAnswer: Correct, and out of order. Urgency is very likely the right conclusion, and the question asks for the method.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: The researcher's clock is not FinCorp's risk basis.

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | CA-5 Plan of Action and Milestones; RA-7 Risk Response
NIST SP 800-115 | Chapter 8 Post-Testing Activities

questions.question: Which gap in the testing program MOST directly allowed the flaw to reach production?

options.A: The team skipped regression testing, so a previously fixed defect returned unnoticed.
options.B: The team skipped unit testing, so individual functions went unverified in isolation.
options.C: The team performed happy-path tests and left invalid or hostile input untried.
options.D: The team skipped load testing, so behavior under peak transaction volume was unknown.

questions.explanation:
Valid deposits were tested and they worked. Nobody exercised an amount outside the legitimate range, and that is negative, edge-case testing (C).
Happy-path success says nothing about how software treats input it was never meant to receive.
questions.recallLine: FinCorp's deposit feature accepted a check amount of minus one hundred. Which testing-program gap MOST directly allowed that flaw to reach production?

optionsShort.A: Skipped regression testing, a fixed defect returned
optionsShort.B: Skipped unit testing, functions unverified in isolation
optionsShort.C: Happy-path tests, hostile input untried
optionsShort.D: Skipped load testing, peak-volume behavior unknown

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Fails on the timeline. Regression testing guards working behavior against new changes; this flaw shipped in the first release.

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: Misplaces the cause. Unit tests verify what developers specified, and the specification omitted invalid amounts.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Addresses volume and concurrency. This defect appears at any transaction rate.

questions.question: Which term BEST describes the portal engagement as directed?

options.A: A white-box engagement, since testers can observe every response the portal returns.
options.B: A black-box engagement, since testers start with no internal knowledge of the target.
options.C: A gray-box engagement, since the public URL constitutes a grant of partial internal knowledge.
options.D: A design review, since the portal's exposed interface reveals its architecture.

questions.explanation:
The testers begin with zero internal knowledge - a public URL and nothing else - and that is what the classification turns on. Black-box (B), chosen precisely to reproduce an uninformed external attacker's view.
Classify tests by what the testers are given, never by what they manage to discover.
questions.recallLine: Testers of Kingsmere's customer portal receive only the public address, with no credentials, diagrams or code. Which term BEST describes the engagement?

optionsShort.A: White-box, since every response is observable
optionsShort.B: Black-box, since testers begin with nothing internal
optionsShort.C: Gray-box, since a public URL grants partial knowledge
optionsShort.D: Design review, since the interface reveals architecture

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Misreads white-box, which means testers are handed internals. Observable responses confer no inside knowledge.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: Implies deliberately granted partial internals, such as an account or diagrams. A public URL is available to everyone.

D.label: wrong phase
D.wouldAnswer: Evaluates documentation, and the target here is live. No documentation was provided either.

questions.question: What issue does that server sitting unassessed for months illustrate?

options.A: A false positive: the scanner reported findings that did not actually exist.
options.B: A false negative: the scanner examined the server but failed to recognize the flaws present.
options.C: A true negative: the scanner correctly determined the server was not vulnerable.
options.D: A coverage gap: the server was outside scan scope, so no result exists for it.

questions.explanation:
A result can only be true or false if the control actually examined the target. This server was removed from scope, so the scanner produced no result about it at all. That is a coverage gap (D), and clean-looking reports then concealed it.
Scope errors are silent. Validate what a scan covered before trusting what it concluded.
questions.recallLine: A firewall change dropped a new application server's subnet from the scanner's target list for months. What issue does the episode illustrate?

optionsShort.A: False positive: findings reported that did not exist
optionsShort.B: False negative: server tested, its flaws missed
optionsShort.C: True negative: server correctly judged not vulnerable
optionsShort.D: Coverage gap: server unscanned, so no result

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Describes a reported finding that turns out to be untrue. Nothing was reported here.

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: Requires the scanner to have tested the server and missed the flaw. It never tested it.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Correct determination of no vulnerability, and here no determination occurred.

questions.question: How should the injection finding be classified, given the retest?

options.A: A true positive that must remain open until the vendor confirms the patch.
options.B: A false negative that indicates the scanner's plugins are out of date.
options.C: A false positive: the scanner alerted on a vulnerability that is not present.
options.D: A true negative, reflecting the parameter's correct, safe, and verified implementation.

questions.explanation:
The tool asserted a vulnerability. Independent verification - parameterized code, plus a failed manual proof-of-concept - shows the assertion was wrong. An alert on a condition that is absent is a false positive (C).
Classify results on two axes: what the tool said, and what is actually true.
questions.recallLine: A scanner flagged a critical injection flaw that parameterized code and a failed manual proof-of-concept both refute. How should the finding be classified?

optionsShort.A: True positive, open until the vendor patches
optionsShort.B: False negative, showing plugins are out of date
optionsShort.C: False positive: alerted on an absent vulnerability
optionsShort.D: True negative, reflecting a safe verified implementation

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Requires the flaw to exist, and the retest demonstrates it does not.

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: The mirror image: a real flaw the tool missed. Plugin currency has nothing to do with over-reporting.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: Would mean the scanner correctly reported the parameter clean. It reported the opposite.

questions.question: How should the weekly log review be categorized in the framework?

options.A: Detective, because it identifies security events after they have taken place.
options.B: Preventive, because publicizing the review deters would-be insiders from attempting fraudulent transactions.
options.C: Corrective, because reviewers restore the accounts affected by fraudulent activity.
options.D: Compensating, because it substitutes for transaction controls Ravenscar Building Society lacks.

questions.explanation:
The review identifies fraud after the transactions complete. It changes knowledge, and it changes no outcome, which puts it squarely in the detective category (A).
Categorize a control by what it does by itself: detect, prevent, or correct. Do not classify by what its output later enables.
questions.recallLine: A regulator asked Ravenscar to place its weekly application-log review, which spots fraud after transactions complete and halts none, within a control framework. Which category fits?

optionsShort.A: Detective, identifying events once they have occurred
optionsShort.B: Preventive, since publicity deters would-be insiders
optionsShort.C: Corrective, since reviewers restore affected accounts
optionsShort.D: Compensating, standing in for missing transaction controls

B.label: wrong phase
B.wouldAnswer: Describes a deterrent effect, a different category. A preventive control would stop the transaction completing.

C.label: correct but not first
C.wouldAnswer: Describes what happens in response to what the review finds. Restoring accounts is a separate corrective activity.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Would require a primary control that cannot be implemented, and nothing here says transaction controls are absent.

questions.question: Which measure BEST addresses counsel's requirement on the audit trail?

options.A: Encrypting the log archive so its contents stay confidential while in storage.
options.B: Writing logs to write-once storage with integrity verification outside admin control.
options.C: Replicating the logs to a second data center so they survive a site failure.
options.D: Restricting log queries to the investigation team for the duration of the case.

questions.explanation:
For evidence to survive challenge, the bank has to show tamper-resistance against every actor, its own administrators included. Write-once storage with integrity verification held outside admin control (B) makes post-write alteration technically infeasible and independently checkable.
Map the requirement to the property it names. Counsel asked for integrity, so the control has to make modification impossible or detectable.
questions.recallLine: Counsel needs the audit trail shown to be unaltered after writing, including by the administrators who run the logging platform. Which measure BEST meets that?

optionsShort.A: Encrypt the archive so contents stay confidential
optionsShort.B: Write-once storage, integrity checks outside admin control
optionsShort.C: Replicate the logs to a second data center
optionsShort.D: Restrict log queries to the investigation team

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Protects confidentiality. An administrator with the keys can still decrypt, alter and re-encrypt.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Protects availability. It faithfully copies tampered records to the second site.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: Limits who reads the logs and does nothing about privileged writes or deletions underneath.

questions.question: Which monitoring approach BEST meets the overnight end-to-end requirement?

options.A: Scripted synthetic transactions that exercise the deposit workflow on a fixed schedule.
options.B: Real user monitoring that measures the sessions of actual customers as they occur.
options.C: A weekly credentialed vulnerability scan of the servers behind the deposit service.
options.D: Quarterly regression testing of the deposit code in the staging environment.

questions.explanation:
Detecting a failure at 3 a.m. before customers do requires traffic that exists at 3 a.m. Scripted synthetic transactions (A) run the deposit journey on a schedule and alert the moment one fails.
Active monitoring answers whether it works right now. Passive monitoring answers what users experienced.
questions.recallLine: Operations want proof the deposit service works end to end at three in the morning, before a customer meets an error. Which monitoring approach BEST fits?

optionsShort.A: Scripted journeys run on a fixed schedule
optionsShort.B: Real user monitoring of live customer sessions
optionsShort.C: Weekly credentialed vulnerability scan of the servers
optionsShort.D: Quarterly regression testing in the staging environment

B.label: wrong phase
B.wouldAnswer: Passive. With no users active it has nothing to measure, and the users who do arrive become the victims.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Assesses security posture on a weekly cadence and reveals nothing about transaction health in the moment.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: Validates code changes in staging. Tonight's production availability is a different question.

questions.question: Which report BEST meets the need for twelve months of operating effectiveness?

options.A: A SOC 1 Type II report on the controls relevant to financial reporting.
options.B: A SOC 2 Type I report on the design of security controls at year-end.
options.C: A SOC 3 report, which is intended for unrestricted general distribution.
options.D: A SOC 2 Type II report covering control operation over the review period.

questions.explanation:
Three requirements decide it. Security and availability point to the Trust Services Criteria, so SOC 2. Operating effectiveness across twelve months requires testing over a period, so Type II. Auditor-level detail requires the full restricted report. Only the SOC 2 Type II report (D) satisfies all three.
Map the subject matter to the SOC series, and the time dimension to the type.
questions.recallLine: Colebrook wants third-party assurance that a provider's security and availability controls worked across twelve months, detailed enough for its own auditors. Which report BEST meets that?

optionsShort.A: SOC 1 Type II on financial-reporting controls
optionsShort.B: SOC 2 Type I on control design at year-end
optionsShort.C: SOC 3, a general-distribution summary
optionsShort.D: SOC 2 Type II covering operation over the period

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: The SOC 1 series addresses controls relevant to a customer's financial reporting.

B.label: wrong phase
B.wouldAnswer: Opines on control design at a single date and says nothing about how the controls operated over the year.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: General-use summary, stripped of the testing detail Colebrook Payments's auditors need.

questions.question: A single executive was able to waive security review to protect a launch date. Which control should the CISO recommend?

options.A: Scheduling an independent penetration test of each new release soon after it reaches production.
options.B: An enforced SDLC gate whose security criteria and waiver authority sit outside the project.
options.C: A larger regression suite covering the security defects discovered in each previous release.
options.D: Real-time monitoring dashboards giving executives immediate visibility of security incidents in production.

questions.explanation:
The control failure was governance, so the fix has to relocate authority. A gate whose pass criteria are defined in advance, and whose waiver requires formal risk acceptance outside the project (B), makes skipping security a decision the project cannot take alone.
When a control can be waived by the person it constrains, the defect is the waiver path. The correction is separation of authority.
questions.recallLine: A single executive was able to waive security review to protect a launch date. Which control should the CISO recommend?

optionsShort.A: Independent penetration test soon after each release
optionsShort.B: Enforced SDLC gate, waiver authority outside the project
optionsShort.C: Bigger regression suite covering past security defects
optionsShort.D: Real-time dashboards showing executives production incidents

A.label: detective when preventive is asked
A.wouldAnswer: Happens after exposure begins, however independent the tester. The VP could still ship unreviewed.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Re-checks known defects. This flaw was unknown, and no test suite constrains an executive's waiver power.

D.label: symptom not cause
D.wouldAnswer: Informs after release. Visibility is not authority.

questions.question: Which change BEST implements shifting security work earlier in practice?

options.A: Adding threat modeling and static analysis to the earliest development phases.
options.B: Increasing the frequency of production penetration tests from yearly to quarterly.
options.C: Moving the security team's reviews to the final gate before each release.
options.D: Expanding post-launch monitoring so exploitation is detected within minutes.

questions.explanation:
Shifting left means moving security activity toward the early phases, where the review found fixes cost minutes instead of millions. In practice that is threat modeling and static analysis at design and coding time (A).
The economics in the stem are the whole argument. Each phase earlier multiplies the fix-cost advantage, so put the effort where the defect is cheapest to kill.
questions.recallLine: A defect at Ellesmere would have cost minutes at design, days at code review and millions after launch. Which change BEST implements shifting security work earlier?

optionsShort.A: Threat modeling and static analysis in early phases
optionsShort.B: Production penetration tests quarterly instead of yearly
optionsShort.C: Security review moved to the final release gate
optionsShort.D: Expanded post-launch monitoring detecting exploitation within minutes

B.label: wrong phase
B.wouldAnswer: Still finds flaws after they are built and shipped, however often it runs. That is the expensive end of the timeline.

C.label: wrong phase
C.wouldAnswer: The rightmost point before launch, and the position whose waiver started this story.

D.label: detective when preventive is asked
D.wouldAnswer: Accepts the flaw's arrival in production and optimizes the response to it.

questions.question: Which procedure provides the MOST direct evidence that role separation holds?

options.A: Logging in as a technician and attempting each administrator function in a controlled test.
options.B: Reading the role-assignment policy and confirming it defines the separation correctly.
options.C: Interviewing the console administrators about whether technicians have ever exceeded their assigned role.
options.D: Confirming that the console vendor's SOC 2 report covers logical access controls in scope.

questions.explanation:
Documents and testimony describe how access control is supposed to work. Exercising the system shows how it does work. Log in as a technician and attempt each administrator function in a controlled test (A), and the evidence is direct and first-hand.
Audit evidence has a hierarchy: testing above inspection, inspection above inquiry. Reach for the highest class the engagement allows.
questions.recallLine: An auditor must verify that a field-technician login cannot invoke the restricted administrator functions on the machine management console. Which procedure gives the MOST direct evidence?

optionsShort.A: Log in as a technician and attempt each admin function
optionsShort.B: Read the role-assignment policy and confirm it defines separation
optionsShort.C: Interview administrators about technicians exceeding their role
optionsShort.D: Check the vendor's SOC 2 covers logical access

B.label: wrong phase
B.wouldAnswer: Verifies design intent. The auditor's question is about operation.

C.label: correct but not first
C.wouldAnswer: Collects assertions, the weakest evidence class, useful mainly for corroboration.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: The vendor's SOC 2 report attests to the vendor's own organization and generic product controls, whatever its stated scope.

questions.question: Which approach BEST supports a defensible conclusion within the audit window?

options.A: Reviewing the records from the department where problems surfaced before.
options.B: Reviewing the most recent month's records and extrapolating to the full year.
options.C: Selecting a statistically representative sample of records across the whole population.
options.D: Asking each manager to self-certify their own reviews and tallying the responses.

questions.explanation:
A defensible conclusion about 12,000 records in limited time is what statistical sampling provides. A representative selection across the whole population (C) supports an inference about all of it, with quantifiable confidence.
When full-population testing is impossible, the defensibility of the conclusion comes from how the sample was drawn.
questions.recallLine: An internal auditor must verify 12,000 access-review sign-offs in a window too short to check every record. Which approach BEST supports a defensible conclusion?

optionsShort.A: Review the department where problems surfaced before
optionsShort.B: Review the latest month and extrapolate to the year
optionsShort.C: Statistically representative sample across the whole population
optionsShort.D: Ask each manager to self-certify their own reviews

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: Samples where problems already surfaced, which biases the result and supports no conclusion about the rest.

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: Convenience sample. Sign-off discipline in December says little about March.

D.label: not the decision-maker's
D.wouldAnswer: Replaces independent verification with the auditee's own assertion, the conflict of interest audits exist to avoid.

questions.question: What is the MOST likely basis for the customers rejecting the internal assessment?

options.A: The internal report is confidential and may not lawfully be shared outside Ellesmere Trust.
options.B: The internal team used sampling, and the customers require full-population testing.
options.C: An assessment by Ellesmere Trust's own staff lacks the independence third parties require.
options.D: The internal audit examined control design but could not test operating effectiveness.

questions.explanation:
Third parties discount even excellent internal work for a structural reason: the assessor is employed by the organization being assessed (C). No thoroughness of working papers cures the relationship.
Internal audit's independence is organizational: it reports inside the company, ideally to the audit committee. Assurance that has to cross a company boundary needs a third party's opinion.
questions.recallLine: Payment-processor customers reject the trust's internal assessments even though the working papers are thorough and the findings candid. What MOST likely explains the rejection?

optionsShort.A: The report is confidential and may not be shared
optionsShort.B: The team sampled; customers require full-population testing
optionsShort.C: Own staff assessing themselves lacks the required independence
optionsShort.D: Internal audit tested design, not operating effectiveness

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Misstates the barrier. Internal reports can be shared under agreement; confidentiality is a choice.

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: Fails because external auditors sample too. Sampling methodology is standard practice.

D.label: wrong phase
