profile.environment: Automated pipeline, twenty production deploys a day · manual security review before each audit
profile.state: Rewritten authentication service ready to ship

stimuli.title: A flaw in a library everybody uses
stimuli.text: A critical flaw is announced in a widely used open-source logging library, and exploitation is already being reported. Global Bank runs four hundred applications and cannot say within hours which of them embed a vulnerable version, including the dependencies pulled in automatically during builds. In the same week a network-management vendor discloses that its customers were breached through a signed, official product update: investigators found the vendor's build server had been compromised months before. And the bank's own VPN appliance carries an actively exploited flaw for which the manufacturer says no patch will exist for several weeks.

profile.environment: Open-source logging library in unknown numbers of builds · vendor-supplied VPN appliance
profile.state: Flaw announced, exploitation already reported

stimuli.title: Two hundred services, no shared plumbing
stimuli.text: Trellis Pay is moving its payments backend off self-managed virtual machines. Two hundred microservices call each other directly, and security now requires mutual TLS and per-call authorization between every pair; modifying two hundred codebases has been ruled out as infeasible. A review of the container platform finds application containers running as root, built from unscanned images pulled from public registries, on shared hosts. A document-processing workload is moving to a serverless functions platform. The architects want the new payment API's threats enumerated before code is written, and the API it replaces is already taking millions of requests enumerating sequential customer identifiers, with stolen credential lists replayed against its login.

profile.environment: Two hundred microservices · container platform on shared hosts · serverless functions
profile.state: Moving off self-managed virtual machines

stimuli.title: A first application security lead
stimuli.text: Global Bank has hired its first application security lead into a company with no existing program, a small training budget and no secure-coding standard, and the lead must choose a starting point for developer training. A threat-modeling workshop for the trading platform has just produced forty distinct threats, far more than the team can address this quarter, and the lead needs a repeatable way to decide which ones get remediation effort first. A separate review is examining an episode in which a master API key became readable by anyone browsing a public repository, and is classifying each event in it.

profile.organization: Global Bank · new application security function
profile.environment: No existing program · small training budget · trading platform under review
profile.state: Lead in post four weeks

stimuli.title: Three incidents on the store estate
stimuli.text: Vantage Retail's in-store machines run a fixed, unchanging set of approved applications and staff cannot administer them. The security team is reviewing three incidents from the quarter. On one server, firewall logs show connections that no local tool reports: process listings, file searches and the installed antivirus all show nothing unusual. Antivirus quarantines one variant of a malware family, yet new infections keep appearing, each sample carrying a different hash and byte pattern while behaving identically on the host. And help-desk tickets reveal that several employees installed a free PDF converter which works as advertised and also opens a remote-control channel.

profile.environment: Fixed set of approved applications · staff cannot administer their machines
profile.state: Quarterly incident review

stimuli.title: An overnight spread, and two peer reports
stimuli.text: Overnight, malware spread to hundreds of Halden Logistics servers across a flat internal network while no user was logged in anywhere: each infected host scanned for neighbors exposing the same vulnerable file-sharing service and infected them directly. Through the sector information-sharing group it belongs to, the company received two reports the same week. A university network team traced abuse complaints to two hundred campus workstations making identical periodic connections to one overseas domain from which they fetch commands. A hospital paid attackers to recover encrypted patient records. An analyst is separately classifying code that appends itself to spreadsheet macro files.

profile.environment: Hundreds of servers on one flat segment · two peer reports received the same week
profile.state: Spread contained, committee prioritizing

stimuli.title: Global Bank: the reporting warehouse
stimuli.text: Global Bank's reporting warehouse serves branch operations, fraud analytics and its cash-in-transit contractor from one database. A customer's mailing address differs across three tables: an update routine changed one copy and missed the others, and refunds are being posted to an outdated address. The fraud reporting view hides individual case records but permits statistical queries. The contractor holds access to three datasets each rated non-sensitive on its own: vehicle maintenance schedules, fuel purchases and crew duty rosters. Nobody has reviewed what those three together would tell a reader, because each was approved on its own rating.

profile.environment: One database serving branch operations, fraud analytics and a logistics contractor
profile.state: Data-quality review after misdirected refunds

questions.question: The examiner wants evidence that the pipeline enforces the bank's rules instead of merely documenting them. Which approach BEST produces that evidence?

options.A: A quarterly audit sampling merged changes against the written development standard.
options.B: A checklist each team lead signs before a release is promoted into production.
options.C: Policy expressed as machine-checked pipeline rules that fail the build and record the result.
options.D: A dashboard showing how many findings each team closed in the most recent release.

questions.explanation:
An examiner asking for enforcement wants something that cannot have been skipped, and a rule that runs is the only artifact on this list with that property (C). It also produces its own evidence as a by-product, which is the second half of what was asked.
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 SC-50 Software-Enforced Separation and Policy Enforcement is the nearest control in the catalog, and it is new in Revision 5. CM-6 Configuration Settings governs the settings the rules assert, and NIST SP 800-218 PO.3.3 requires the toolchain to be configured to generate artifacts that support the security checks. Be precise about one thing: the phrase software-defined security appears in no NIST document, so SC-50 is a functional match, and it should be presented that way.
Evidence is what the machine produced.
questions.recallLine: An examiner wants proof the pipeline enforces the rules and not documenting them. What produces it?

optionsShort.A: Quarterly audit sampling merges
optionsShort.B: Team lead checklist before promotion
optionsShort.C: Machine-checked rules that fail builds
optionsShort.D: Dashboard of findings closed

A.label: detective when preventive is asked
A.wouldAnswer: Detective when preventive is asked, sampling a quarter after the fact.

B.label: symptom not cause
B.wouldAnswer: Captures a person's assertion. The stem asks for an enforced condition.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Measures remediation throughput, not whether any rule was applied.

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | SC-50 Software-Enforced Separation and Policy Enforcement (new in Rev 5); CM-6 Configuration Settings
NIST SP 800-218 | PO.3.3 toolchain generates supporting artifacts

questions.question: Any team can queue work on the shared build runners. Which risk does that arrangement MOST directly create for the Cardless Cash release?

options.A: One team's build step can read another team's secrets or artifacts.
options.B: Builds will queue behind each other and the weekly release will slip.
options.C: Teams will adopt different build tools and the artifacts will diverge.
options.D: The runners will fall behind on operating-system patches between releases.

questions.explanation:
A build runner holds every credential its jobs need and every artifact they produce, and a shared runner holds all of them at once. A job is arbitrary code by definition, so the team that queues it inherits whatever the runner can reach (A). The vault the bank has just bought stops helping the moment a job can ask the vault on someone else's behalf.
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AC-6 Least Privilege, SC-2 Separation of System and User Functionality, and SC-4 Information in Shared System Resources name this class of exposure. Note that SC-2's Revision 4 title was Application Partitioning. NIST SP 800-218 PO.5 requires environments involved in software development to be separated and protected.
Ask what the runner can reach.
questions.recallLine: Any team can queue jobs on shared build runners. Which risk does that most directly create?

optionsShort.A: Cross-team access to secrets and artifacts
optionsShort.B: Queueing delays the weekly release
optionsShort.C: Divergent build tools between teams
optionsShort.D: Runners fall behind on patching

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: A capacity concern. Queueing delays a release and crosses no boundary.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: A consistency issue between teams, and no boundary failure inside one runner.

D.label: correct but not first
D.wouldAnswer: A real maintenance gap that shared queueing did not cause.

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | AC-6 Least Privilege; SC-2 Separation of System and User Functionality (renamed from Rev 4 Application Partitioning); SC-4 Information in Shared System Resources
NIST SP 800-218 | PO.5 secure development environments

questions.question: The key is still live and the repository is still public. What should the team do FIRST?

options.A: Delete the offending file from the repository and rewrite its commit history to purge the key
options.B: Make the repository private so that no additional external parties can view the key
options.C: Revoke the exposed key immediately and issue a replacement through approved channels
options.D: Interview the developer to establish how the key came to be committed and pushed

questions.explanation:
Automated bots scrape public repositories for credential patterns within seconds of a push. After three days, the only safe assumption is that the key has already been copied. Nothing that changes who can see the repository going forward alters that, so make the stolen value worthless first: revoke and reissue through a proper channel (C), then hunt for fraudulent use during the exposure window.
Containment comes before cleanup, and before understanding.
questions.recallLine: A production API key with administrative access has sat in a public repository for three days. What should the team do FIRST?

optionsShort.A: Delete the file and rewrite commit history
optionsShort.B: Make the repository private
optionsShort.C: Revoke the key and reissue it
optionsShort.D: Interview the developer about the commit

A.label: symptom not cause
A.wouldAnswer: Treats the visible symptom. It cannot recall the copies already harvested, and leaves an active credential live meanwhile.

B.label: symptom not cause
B.wouldAnswer: Fails the same way. Private visibility stops future viewers and does nothing about what is already copied.

D.label: correct but not first
D.wouldAnswer: Matters for the lessons learned and for fixing the process. Root-cause interviews come after containment.

questions.question: Commits containing secrets must be blocked before they reach the central repository, in a way an individual developer cannot bypass from their own machine. Which mechanism BEST meets this?

options.A: A server-side pre-receive hook that scans incoming pushes and rejects any containing secrets
options.B: A client-side pre-commit hook on every developer workstation that runs local secret scanning
options.C: A nightly scheduled job that scans the repository contents and alerts on any secrets found
options.D: A mandatory code-review checklist item requiring reviewers to look for embedded credentials

questions.explanation:
The requirement has two halves: enforcement before the secret enters the shared repository, and enforcement developers cannot switch off. Only a control running on the server satisfies both. A pre-receive hook (A) evaluates every push at the moment the server is asked to accept it and refuses the whole push if a secret is detected. Nothing to install, nothing to bypass.
A guarantee of the form 'never enters the repository' can only be enforced where the repository lives.
questions.recallLine: Commits carrying secrets must be blocked before they reach the bank's central repository, unbypassable from a developer's own machine. Which mechanism BEST meets this?

optionsShort.A: Server-side pre-receive hook rejecting pushes containing secrets
optionsShort.B: Client-side pre-commit hook on each workstation
optionsShort.C: Nightly scan of repository contents, alerting
optionsShort.D: Code-review checklist item for embedded credentials

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: The closest wrong answer. Client hooks live on machines the developer controls: a flag skips them, a fresh clone lacks them.

C.label: detective when preventive is asked
C.wouldAnswer: Too late. By the nightly run the secret has been in shared history for hours, cloned and mirrored.

D.label: wrong phase
D.wouldAnswer: Relies on human review, and in pull-request workflows the code reaches the server before anyone reviews it.

questions.question: Investigators establish the attackers were active for five months and no alert ever fired. Which improvement should the security program prioritize?

options.A: Deploying stronger encryption for stored data so future intrusions yield nothing readable
options.B: Centralized log collection with longer retention and automated alerting on suspicious activity
options.C: Commissioning an annual external penetration test to uncover exploitable weaknesses
options.D: Adopting a stricter rotation schedule for all privileged administrator account passwords

questions.explanation:
Five months of undetected activity is a visibility failure, and the stem lists its three ingredients: logs that expire in a week, security-relevant events never captured, and review too infrequent and manual to notice anything. Centralized collection with longer retention and automated alerting attacks all three (B). Collect logs centrally where intruders cannot quietly erase them, retain them well beyond realistic dwell times so investigations have evidence, and let automation watch continuously, so detection happens in hours.
Long dwell times indict detection. Build logging and monitoring before buying more prevention.
questions.recallLine: Attackers worked inside Coastal Savings' payment API for five months and no alert ever fired. Which improvement should the security program prioritize?

optionsShort.A: Stronger encryption for stored data
optionsShort.B: Central logs, longer retention, automated alerting
optionsShort.C: An annual external penetration test
optionsShort.D: Stricter rotation of privileged account passwords

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Protects confidentiality against stolen media. Attackers using compromised accounts read data exactly as users do.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: A point-in-time probe for ways in. The demonstrated failure is not knowing when someone is already inside.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Nothing in the incident ties it to stale passwords, and rotation would not have surfaced a five-month presence.

questions.question: Simply viewing a certain product review causes browsers to send their session cookies to an unknown domain; script tags stored in the review text are rendered verbatim to every visitor. Which remediation MOST directly addresses this?

options.A: Add anti-forgery tokens to every state-changing form so requests from other sites are rejected
options.B: Move all pages to HTTPS so session cookies are protected from network eavesdropping
options.C: Use parameterized queries so review text is treated as data, not command structure
options.D: Encode user-supplied content on output so browsers render it as text as opposed to script

questions.explanation: This is stored cross-site scripting. Attacker-supplied markup was saved and later delivered into victims' pages, where the browser executed it. The defect sits at the rendering step, so the direct fix is contextual output encoding (D): the stored text displays as inert characters and is never parsed as script. A Content Security Policy and HttpOnly cookies add depth.
questions.recallLine: Script tags stored in a product review render verbatim and send every viewer's session cookie to an unknown domain. Which remediation MOST directly addresses this?

optionsShort.A: Anti-forgery tokens on state-changing forms
optionsShort.B: Move all portal pages to HTTPS
optionsShort.C: Parameterized queries for stored review text
optionsShort.D: Encode user content on output as text

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Counters CSRF, where an attacker forges requests using the victim's session. Here the attacker injected script.

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Protects cookies in transit. These are read by script running inside the page itself, over any transport.

C.label: wrong phase
C.wouldAnswer: Stops SQL injection. The review was stored through a legitimate write, and the database behaved correctly.

questions.question: A crash dump shows an oversized message-length field overwriting the C daemon's return address, after which the service executed attacker-supplied instructions. Which change BEST addresses the root cause?

options.A: Validate length fields and use bounds-checked memory operations for every buffer write
options.B: Enable address space layout randomization so injected code lands at unpredictable locations
options.C: Filter inbound packets at the network firewall to drop traffic from untrusted address ranges
options.D: Raise the service's logging level so malformed packets are recorded for later investigation

questions.explanation:
A buffer overflow happens when code writes more data into a buffer than was allocated, corrupting adjacent memory, here the saved return address. The root cause is the unchecked write, so the fix is in the code (A): validate untrusted length fields and use bounds-checked operations so an oversized value can no longer spill past the buffer. Migrating hot paths to a memory-safe language is the same idea taken further.
Mitigations raise attacker cost. Only correct code removes the vulnerability.
questions.recallLine: An oversized message-length field overwrote the C daemon's return address and the service then ran attacker instructions. Which change BEST addresses the root cause?

optionsShort.A: Validate lengths and bounds-check every buffer write
optionsShort.B: Enable ASLR so injected code lands unpredictably
optionsShort.C: Drop untrusted address ranges at the firewall
optionsShort.D: Raise logging so malformed packets are recorded

B.label: symptom not cause
B.wouldAnswer: An exploit mitigation. ASLR makes a successful overflow harder to weaponize and leaves the defect in place.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: The service must accept client packets to function, and any permitted source can send the malformed field.

D.label: detective when preventive is asked
D.wouldAnswer: Detective when preventive is asked. Logging records the compromise after it has happened.

questions.question: An uploaded invoice whose DOCTYPE declaration defines an external entity pointing at /etc/passwd returns that file's contents. Which change BEST fixes this flaw at its source?

options.A: Validate that uploaded invoices are well-formed XML before passing them to the parser
options.B: Configure the XML parser to disable document type definitions and external entity resolution
options.C: Run the upload service in a container so its file reads are confined to the container image
options.D: Scan uploaded files with antivirus to reject those containing known malicious markup

questions.explanation:
XML external entity injection is unusual among injection flaws: the vulnerability is a feature. The parser does exactly what DTD processing specifies and resolves an entity that happens to point at a local file. So the source-level fix is configuration (B). Turn off DTDs and external entity resolution, and the attack stops being expressible.
When a parser's features are the attack surface, harden its configuration. The lesson generalizes to any dangerous default.
questions.recallLine: An uploaded invoice whose DOCTYPE points at /etc/passwd returns that file's contents to the supplier. Which change BEST fixes the flaw at its source?

optionsShort.A: Check uploads are well-formed XML first
optionsShort.B: Disable DTDs and entity resolution
optionsShort.C: Run the upload service in a container
optionsShort.D: Antivirus-scan uploads for malicious markup

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: Checks syntax, and the exploit file is perfectly well-formed XML. This attack is syntactically impeccable.

C.label: symptom not cause
C.wouldAnswer: Shrinks the blast radius and leaves the flaw. Container secrets stay readable and entity fetches still reach the network.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: Recognizes known malware. A three-line DOCTYPE crafted for this one application matches nothing in a signature set.

questions.question: Which pair of cookie attributes MOST directly closes the script-access and unencrypted-transport exposures together?

options.A: Domain and Path, which limit the hosts and URL prefixes to which the cookie is sent
options.B: HttpOnly and Secure, which deny script access and restrict the cookie to encrypted transport
options.C: Max-Age and Expires, which bound how long the browser retains the session cookie
options.D: SameSite and Path, which control whether cross-site navigation includes the cookie

questions.explanation: Map each finding to the attribute built for it. HttpOnly hides the cookie from the page's JavaScript, so even a successful XSS payload cannot read it. Secure forbids the browser from sending the cookie over anything but an encrypted connection. HttpOnly and Secure carry both (B).
questions.recallLine: Kestrel Mutual's session cookie is readable by page scripts and travels over plain HTTP. Which pair of cookie attributes MOST directly closes both exposures?

optionsShort.A: Domain and Path, scoping hosts and prefixes
optionsShort.B: HttpOnly and Secure, denying scripts and cleartext
optionsShort.C: Max-Age and Expires, bounding cookie lifetime
optionsShort.D: SameSite and Path, governing cross-site navigation

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: Scopes which requests include the cookie. Within that scope, scripts can still read it and HTTP links still carry it.

C.label: symptom not cause
C.wouldAnswer: Shrinks the window of misuse and closes neither exposure. A cookie can be stolen or sniffed in its first minute.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: SameSite governs whether cross-site requests attach the cookie, a CSRF defense. Neither finding is cross-site.

questions.question: Leadership wants working software delivered early and refined continuously from real user feedback. Which approach BEST fits the consumer feature?

options.A: Waterfall, since completing the full design before coding avoids expensive rework later
options.B: Cleanroom, since formally verified increments give the highest confidence in each release
options.C: Agile, since short iterations and continuous customer feedback absorb changing requirements
options.D: The V-model, since pairing every build phase with a matching test phase catches defects early

questions.explanation: Rapidly shifting requirements plus a demand for early, continuously refined releases are the exact conditions iterative Agile methods were created for (C). Each short cycle delivers working software and folds user feedback into the next.
questions.recallLine: Leadership wants the new consumer feature delivered early and refined continuously from real user feedback in a market that shifts every few weeks. Which approach fits BEST?

optionsShort.A: Waterfall, full design completed before coding
optionsShort.B: Cleanroom, formally verified increments each release
optionsShort.C: Agile, short iterations absorbing changing requirements
optionsShort.D: V-model, each build phase paired with testing

A.label: wrong phase
A.wouldAnswer: Assumes requirements can be fixed before design begins. Here they cannot, so the design describes the wrong product.

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Slow, and it assumes a precise spec exists. Cleanroom's formal verification suits safety-critical software.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Still a sequential, plan-driven shape. Its paired test phases verify a fixed specification and cannot absorb change.

questions.question: The delivery lead wants claims-processing stakeholders to react to something concrete before the team commits to full development. Which approach BEST serves this goal?

options.A: Completing a comprehensive requirements specification and having every stakeholder sign it
options.B: Adopting cleanroom methods so that defects are formally prevented from the earliest phase
options.C: Proceeding directly to full construction so users can react to the finished system itself
options.D: Building a limited working model of the interface for stakeholders to evaluate and refine

questions.explanation:
When stakeholders cannot say what they want, showing beats asking. A prototype gives them something concrete to react to (D), converts vague or contradictory wishes into specific corrections, and costs little enough to throw away and iterate. That is the entire reason prototyping exists as a development approach.
Prototype when requirements are the risk. Formalize when correctness against known requirements is the risk.
questions.recallLine: Claims-processing stakeholders have produced two contradictory requirements documents. Which approach BEST gives them something concrete to react to before the team commits?

optionsShort.A: A comprehensive specification, signed by every stakeholder
optionsShort.B: Cleanroom methods preventing defects formally
optionsShort.C: Proceed directly to full construction
optionsShort.D: A limited working model for stakeholders to evaluate

A.label: symptom not cause
A.wouldAnswer: Doubles down on a technique that has already failed twice. The conflicts resurface as change requests during build.

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Prevents implementation defects. Here the specification is the problem, and a formally verified wrong product is wrong.

C.label: wrong phase
C.wouldAnswer: The largest possible bet on the least information. Feedback arrives after the full cost is sunk.

questions.question: Which pairing of Extreme Programming practices MOST directly catches defects at the moment the code is being written?

options.A: The planning game and small releases, which shorten the feedback loop with customers
options.B: Collective code ownership and coding standards, which keep the code base uniform
options.C: On-site customer and system metaphor, which keep development aligned with business intent
options.D: Pair programming and test-driven development, which review and test code as it is typed

questions.explanation: The discriminator is the moment the code is being written, and two XP practices operate at exactly that instant (D). In test-driven development the failing test exists before the code, so the first run verifies the new logic immediately. In pair programming a second developer reviews each line as it appears, catching slips the author is blind to. Together they are XP's tightest defect-feedback loop.
questions.recallLine: Which pairing of Extreme Programming practices MOST directly catches defects at the moment payment code is being typed?

optionsShort.A: Planning game and small releases
optionsShort.B: Collective ownership and coding standards
optionsShort.C: On-site customer and system metaphor
optionsShort.D: Pair programming and test-driven development

A.label: wrong phase
A.wouldAnswer: Operates at release granularity, surfacing wrong priorities and integration surprises in days or weeks.

B.label: wrong phase
B.wouldAnswer: Improves maintainability and consistency. It examines nothing at the moment the code is created.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Aligns the product with business intent. It catches building the wrong thing, not writing it wrongly.

questions.question: The certifier wants defects prevented during development as opposed to found and patched afterwards, with failure rates certified statistically. Which software engineering approach aligns BEST?

options.A: Extreme Programming, relying on test-driven development and continuous pair review
options.B: Cleanroom engineering, using formal specification, verification, and statistical quality control
options.C: Rapid application development, iterating prototypes quickly until users accept the behavior
options.D: Scrum, delivering the firmware in sprints with a defect backlog groomed by the product owner

questions.explanation: The regulator's two demands are the two pillars of cleanroom software engineering (B). Defects are prevented before test, through formal specification and mathematically based verification of the code. Quality is then demonstrated through statistical usage testing that supports certified reliability claims, which is precisely the evidence sought.
questions.recallLine: The firmware certifier wants defects prevented during development as opposed to patched afterwards, with failure rates certified statistically. Which engineering approach aligns BEST?

optionsShort.A: Extreme Programming, test-driven development and pair review
optionsShort.B: Cleanroom, formal specification, verification, statistical quality control
optionsShort.C: RAD, iterating prototypes until users accept
optionsShort.D: Scrum, sprints with a groomed defect backlog

A.label: detective when preventive is asked
A.wouldAnswer: The strongest wrong answer. TDD and pair review find defects after they are written, and certify no failure rate.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Optimizes speed and user acceptance. RAD's tolerance for rough prototypes is the opposite of certifiable rigor.

D.label: wrong phase
D.wouldAnswer: A management wrapper that routes defects into a backlog for later, and prescribes no engineering rigor at all.

questions.question: The administrator inserts code that will delete the payroll tables if his employee ID ever disappears from the HR system. Which safeguard would MOST likely catch this insertion before it reaches production?

options.A: Antivirus scanning on the database server to detect malicious executable files
options.B: Full-disk encryption of the storage volumes holding the payroll tables
options.C: An annual disaster-recovery exercise proving that payroll can be restored intact from backup tapes
options.D: Mandatory peer review of every code change before it can be merged and deployed

questions.explanation:
This is a logic bomb: legitimate-looking code carrying a malicious trigger. An authorized insider wrote it and it contains no malware signature, so the control most likely to catch it is another human reading the change. Mandatory peer review (D) puts a second set of eyes on a deletion routine conditioned on an HR lookup, an obvious red flag, and its mere existence deters the attempt.
Insider code threats are defeated by process controls on the change pipeline.
questions.recallLine: A departing administrator inserts code that deletes the payroll tables if his employee ID leaves the HR system. Which safeguard would MOST likely catch it beforehand?

optionsShort.A: Antivirus scanning on the database server
optionsShort.B: Full-disk encryption of the payroll volumes
optionsShort.C: An annual disaster-recovery restore exercise
optionsShort.D: Mandatory peer review of every code change

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Hunts foreign binaries. The bomb is source code committed through normal channels.

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Protects confidentiality of data at rest. The bomb deletes through authorized paths that decrypt transparently.

C.label: wrong phase
C.wouldAnswer: Corrective. Recovery exercises limit the damage after detonation rather than prevent it.

questions.question: Every customer who applied the vendor's legitimate update received the implant. Which term BEST describes this attack?

options.A: A watering-hole attack, since victims were compromised at a resource they habitually trust
options.B: Spear phishing, since the malicious payload reached a specifically chosen set of targets
options.C: A supply chain attack, since the vendor's build pipeline was subverted to reach its customers
options.D: An insider threat, since the compromise originated within the vendor's own build systems

questions.explanation:
The attackers never touched the victims directly. They compromised a supplier's build pipeline so the trusted product itself became the delivery vehicle, arriving with a valid signature through the official update channel. That is the definition of a supply chain attack (C), and the SolarWinds pattern precisely. The signature is what makes it devastating: verification passed at every customer, because the code was signed after the implant went in.
When upstream trust is the vector, defenses shift to vendor assurance, build integrity, and monitoring what updates actually do.
questions.recallLine: Every customer that applied a network vendor's signed, official update received an implant planted months earlier on the vendor's build server. Which term BEST describes this?

optionsShort.A: A watering-hole attack on a trusted resource
optionsShort.B: Spear phishing aimed at chosen targets
optionsShort.C: A supply chain attack through the build pipeline
optionsShort.D: An insider threat within the vendor's systems

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: The closest wrong answer. A watering hole poisons a site the targets visit; this poison rode inside a purchased product.

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Works by deceiving chosen individuals. No human was deceived; administrators applied a legitimate update correctly.

D.label: symptom not cause
D.wouldAnswer: Requires an authorized person misusing their own access. Breaching the build server does not make attackers insiders.

questions.question: Which security responsibilities does the team retain once the document-processing workload runs serverless?

options.A: Securing the function code, its dependencies, its secrets, and its least-privilege IAM roles
options.B: Patching the operating system kernels of the servers on which the functions execute
options.C: Hardening the hypervisor layer that isolates the provider's tenants from one another
options.D: Managing host firewalls and antivirus on the machines running the function runtime

questions.explanation: Serverless shifts the shared-responsibility line sharply toward the provider, and never past the customer's own workload. What remains is everything the team writes or configures (A): the function code and its input handling, the third-party dependencies bundled with it, where composition analysis still applies, the secrets it uses, and above all the IAM role it executes under. Over-permissioned functions are the signature serverless failure.
questions.recallLine: The document-processing workload now runs on a serverless functions platform. Which security responsibilities does the Trellis Pay team retain?

optionsShort.A: Function code, dependencies, secrets and IAM roles
optionsShort.B: Patching the kernels of the executing servers
optionsShort.C: Hardening the tenant-isolating hypervisor layer
optionsShort.D: Host firewalls and antivirus on runtime machines

B.label: not the decision-maker's
B.wouldAnswer: In a functions platform the customer cannot reach the operating system, and the provider owns its patching.

C.label: not the decision-maker's
C.wouldAnswer: One layer deeper still. Hypervisor isolation between tenants is the provider's duty in every cloud service model.

D.label: not the decision-maker's
D.wouldAnswer: A responsibility the team held on its old self-managed machines, and would still hold under IaaS.

questions.question: How should the lead BEST use the OWASP Top 10 in building the program?

options.A: Adopt it as the complete set of security requirements the finished application must satisfy
options.B: Treat it as a substitute for penetration testing, since it already lists the likely findings
options.C: Use it as an awareness baseline that focuses training on the most common web risk categories
options.D: Apply it as a hardening checklist for the servers that will host the company's applications

questions.explanation: The OWASP Top 10 is an awareness document, a consensus ranking of the most prevalent categories of web application risk. That makes it an ideal seed for a first training curriculum and coding standard (C): maximum coverage of common failure classes for minimal budget.
questions.recallLine: The new application security lead has a small training budget and no secure-coding standard. How should the lead BEST use the OWASP Top 10?

optionsShort.A: The complete set of requirements the application must satisfy
optionsShort.B: A substitute for penetration testing
optionsShort.C: An awareness baseline focusing training on common risks
optionsShort.D: A hardening checklist for the hosting servers

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: Overstates it. OWASP warns the Top 10 is a starting point; ASVS carries the verification-grade requirements.

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Asks a list of risk categories to examine an implementation. Testing finds the specific instances a list can only name.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: Reaches the wrong layer. Server hardening belongs to configuration baselines such as the CIS Benchmarks.

questions.question: The team suspects kernel-level malware is concealing its presence on that server. What is the MOST reliable way to restore trust in the system?

options.A: Rebuild the system from known-good installation media and restore data from clean backups
options.B: Run a full scan with the installed antivirus using its most aggressive detection settings
options.C: Delete the executables owning the suspicious connections and then reboot the server
options.D: Patch the operating system to the current level so the malware can no longer operate

questions.explanation: A rootkit subverts the operating system itself, so every answer that system gives, from process lists to scan results, is suspect. The firewall seeing traffic the host denies is the classic symptom. Once the kernel is untrusted, the only way to re-establish a trusted computing base is to rebuild from media you trust and restore data verified clean (A).
questions.recallLine: Firewall logs show connections that no tool on the server reports, and kernel-level malware is suspected. What is the MOST reliable way to restore trust?

optionsShort.A: Rebuild from known-good media, restore clean backups
optionsShort.B: Full antivirus scan at aggressive detection settings
optionsShort.C: Delete the suspicious executables and reboot
optionsShort.D: Patch the operating system to current level

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Runs on, and asks questions of, the compromised OS. Aggressive settings do not fix a lying oracle.

C.label: symptom not cause
C.wouldAnswer: The hiding means the owning executables cannot be found reliably, and deleting what is visible leaves the implant.

D.label: wrong phase
D.wouldAnswer: Closes entry vectors for the future. Patching evicts nothing already resident below the tools that would remove it.

questions.question: Each infected server infected its neighbors directly, with no user action anywhere. Which combination of controls BEST limits this class of attack in future?

options.A: Phishing simulations and awareness training so employees stop opening malicious attachments
options.B: Timely patching of exposed network services plus segmentation to contain lateral movement
options.C: Stronger password complexity requirements and lockout thresholds across all accounts
options.D: Full backups of every server retained for ninety days at a separate offsite location

questions.explanation:
Self-propagation through a vulnerable network service with zero user involvement is the signature of a worm, and the stem hands you both contributing causes: an unpatched exposed service, and a flat network where every host can reach every other. Patching removes the exploitable flaw. Segmentation shrinks the population each infected host can even reach. Together (B) they attack propagation at both ends.
Read the propagation mechanism first. It tells you which control family is even in play.
questions.recallLine: Malware spread overnight across Halden Logistics' flat network with nobody logged in, each host infecting neighbors through the same service. Which controls BEST limit this?

optionsShort.A: Phishing simulations and awareness training
optionsShort.B: Timely patching plus network segmentation
optionsShort.C: Stronger password complexity and lockout thresholds
optionsShort.D: Offsite full backups retained ninety days

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Guards the human vector, and the defining clue is that no human acted anywhere in this outbreak.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Hardens credentials, and the worm exploited a service flaw rather than an account.

D.label: wrong phase
D.wouldAnswer: Corrective. Backups rebuild the servers after the damage has been done.

questions.question: By correlating the three datasets the contractor reconstructs the timing and routes of cash-in-transit runs. Which security concern does this BEST illustrate?

options.A: Inference, since the contractor deduced one hidden value from a permitted statistical result
options.B: Collusion, since several parties pooled their separate accesses to reach protected data
options.C: Data remanence, since sensitive residue persisted inside systems rated non-sensitive
options.D: Aggregation, since individually non-sensitive data sets combined into sensitive knowledge

questions.explanation: Every source the contractor touched was legitimately non-sensitive. The classified picture emerged when the sources were correlated. That is aggregation (D): the combination carries a higher sensitivity than any of its parts, which is why access decisions have to consider what a subject can assemble in total, with need-to-know evaluated across holdings.
questions.recallLine: The cash-in-transit contractor correlates maintenance schedules, fuel purchases and duty rosters to reconstruct run timings and routes. Which security concern does this BEST illustrate?

optionsShort.A: Inference, deducing a hidden value from statistics
optionsShort.B: Collusion, parties pooling their separate accesses
optionsShort.C: Data remanence, residue persisting in non-sensitive systems
optionsShort.D: Aggregation, non-sensitive sets combining into sensitive knowledge

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: The closest wrong answer, and the sibling concern. Here nothing was withheld; the sensitivity arose from assembly.

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: Requires multiple actors combining their separate privileges. This was one contractor inside one set of grants.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Data physically surviving on media after deletion or reuse. The databases were serving their intended content.
